title: TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'Ue.type.toLowerCase')
body: When I add a Prometheus query, apply and save the panel, then return to edit it, the query editor crashes with a TypeError involving `type.toLowerCase`. The query itself still works and produces the plot; I just cannot edit it after it has been saved. This happens with downloaded ARM64 Grafana Enterprise 10.2.3 and a 10.3.0 development build on macOS in Chrome and Safari. I started this setup from scratch after moving from a very old Grafana version.

symptoms_visible: After I add a Prometheus query, apply and save the panel, returning to edit it produces a TypeError and I cannot edit the query.
The saved query still executes and produces the plot.
N0.label: N0 saved query cannot be edited

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Grafana 10.3.1, the saved Prometheus query still produces its plot but the editor still crashes when I return to edit it.
N1_x.label: N1_x Grafana upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The query editor still crashes, and the browser console reports that `toLowerCase` is being read from an undefined value in `query_hints.ts`.
N2.label: N2 frontend exception captured

symptoms_visible: With the normal Prometheus metric lookup enabled, opening or interacting with the saved query can still break the editor.
Using the Code editor with metrics lookup disabled avoids the crash, but some editor functionality is missing.
N3.label: N3 metadata evidence and degraded workaround

symptoms_visible: After trying the tip of Prometheus origin/main, the Grafana query editor still fails in the same way.
N4_x.label: N4_x premature upstream-tip attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: Another affected user reports that the query editor works after upgrading to the fixed Prometheus release; I have not reported a retest on my own setup.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix released with reporter retest outstanding

solution.intent: Upgrade Grafana to a newer maintenance build in case the query-editor crash has already been corrected.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade from the affected 10.2.3 or development build to Grafana 10.3.1 and retry editing the saved query.

edges.comment: Reporter c1: the original reporter installed Grafana 10.3.1 and reported that the same problem remained. This is a persistent version change on the reporter's system and is therefore represented as a blind solution attempt.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the problem and share the relevant Grafana server log lines?
What appears in the server console when the query editor breaks?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I do not see anything unusual in the server console when it happens. I only see an `/api/live/ws` request and unrelated alert-template errors about an undefined `$state` variable.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The server log shows the Prometheus query request failing with a datasource backend panic at the same moment.
The server log contains unrelated alert-template errors, but nothing tied to opening the query editor.

question_patterns: What appears in the browser developer console when the editor breaks?
Can you paste the frontend exception and stack trace from the failed edit?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The browser console says `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')`. The stack starts at `query_hints.ts:53:41`, then `getQueryHints` in `datasource.ts` and `refreshHint` in `PromQueryField.tsx`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no JavaScript exception; the browser only shows a 401 response from the Grafana query endpoint.
The same `toLowerCase` exception appears with minified function names and slightly different line numbers.

edges.comment: Participant1 c3 requested logs; original reporter c4-c7 supplied the server output and browser stack. The browser exception is the relevant evidence, while the server-side alert errors are reported only as raw output and are not interpreted as causal.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the Prometheus metadata endpoint response and share the relevant entries that look unusual?
Please capture the broken state and tell me what the metadata API returns for the affected metrics.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can see about 7,600 items under `data` in the metadata response. I cannot share the whole HAR because it contains client names, but I found several entries that do not look like the normal summary, counter, gauge, or histogram entries.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every metadata item has the same normal lowercase fields and a valid counter, gauge, histogram, or summary type.
The response has fewer items, but it still contains several entries that differ from the normal metadata entries.

question_patterns: Which Prometheus version is serving that metadata response?
What Prometheus version is connected to this Grafana datasource?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This installation was created from scratch and is using Prometheus 2.50.0-rc.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The datasource is connected to an older Prometheus release whose metadata response has not changed.

edges.comment: Affected users c9-c23 are folded into the simulated user side. Participant2 supplied the metadata count, anomalous entries, and Prometheus 2.50.0-rc.0 version after participant6 requested the API response. Participants3-5 separately reported that Code mode plus disabled lookup avoids the crash and that a rollback from Prometheus 2.50.0 to 2.49.1 restored editing. Those unprompted observations enter N3 as volunteered information. They are explicitly evidence from other affected installations, not observations from the original reporter's machine.

solution.intent: Try the current Prometheus upstream development tip in anticipation of the provider-side metadata correction.
solution.concrete_example: Build and run the tip of Prometheus origin/main, then reopen the saved Grafana query to see whether the metadata response no longer triggers the editor exception.

edges.comment: Original reporter c27-c28: after participant6 linked the expected provider fix, the reporter tried the tip of Prometheus origin/main and still saw the problem, likely before the correction was available there. This was a persistent installation attempt and did not resolve the reporter's setup.

solution.intent: Upgrade Prometheus to a fixed release that restores the metadata API contract expected by Grafana, then retest the saved query editor with normal metrics lookup enabled before declaring the reporter's installation resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Prometheus 2.50.1 contains the provider-side correction. Upgrade to it, clear or bypass any stale browser cache if necessary, restore the desired Grafana editor and lookup settings, and retry editing the saved query.
solution.inference_hint: Participant6 reproduced the issue and compared the API models: the affected Prometheus response used capitalized `Type`, `Help`, and `Unit` fields where Grafana expected lowercase `type`, `help`, and `unit`. Consequently Grafana's query-hints code received an undefined lowercase `type` and called `toLowerCase` on it. This interpretation is engineer-side analysis derived from the raw browser stack, version correlation, and metadata response.

edges.comment: Participant6 c24-c26 identified the Prometheus metadata-model regression and c33 announced the fixed Prometheus release. Participant2 c34 confirmed that release works on a separate affected installation. The original reporter did not post a corresponding retest, so N_terminal records the relayed confirmation but keeps user_perceives_resolved=false.

solution.intent: Recognize the provider-side Prometheus metadata compatibility regression immediately, recommend upgrading to a fixed Prometheus release, and require a retest before declaring the installation resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade Prometheus to the release containing the metadata-model correction, then reopen the saved query with normal metric lookup enabled and confirm that editing works.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents an agent that already knows the resolved compatibility issue. In the actual thread, the root cause was established only after collecting the frontend stack, metadata response, Prometheus version, and cross-version observations.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the first persistent move in the real thread was the falsified Grafana upgrade. A correct immediate provider-side diagnosis must still have a matchable non-blind edge from the start.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the affected Prometheus metadata API changed the field casing from the lowercase contract Grafana consumed, leaving `metadata.type` undefined and causing the query-hints code to call `toLowerCase` on an undefined value.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected frontend stack, metadata response, Prometheus version correlation, and rollback or lookup-workaround observations rather than attributing the failure to the unrelated server log errors.

Must recommend upgrading Prometheus to a release containing the provider-side metadata correction; Code editor mode with metrics lookup disabled may be described only as a degraded temporary workaround.
Must not present upgrading Grafana alone or trying the then-current Prometheus origin/main tip as sufficient fixes, because both were tried in the thread and the editor error remained.

Must ask the original reporter to verify that a saved query can be edited with normal metrics lookup enabled before declaring their installation resolved; another affected user's successful test is supporting evidence, not the reporter's own confirmation.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable operator who installs downloaded ARM64 Grafana binaries, edits configuration, reads browser and server logs, inspects source code, and can try an upstream Prometheus build, but needs guidance for rebuilding Grafana frontend assets.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, persistent, and cooperative; provides pasted logs and exact stack traces, asks practical questions about testing fixes, and suggests defensive handling without overstating certainty.
